newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS exporting sugar at fast pace - DataNet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS exporting sugar at fast pace - DataNet.

text.p: Sugar exports from Brazil's center-south region are continuing at an intense pace, according to independent consultant DataNet-Agricommodities.

As of September 30, there were 18 sugar ships docked in Santos, 15 of which were loading bagged sugar, while in Paranagua four ships were taking on sugar and a further seven were waiting entry into the port, the company said in its weekly report.

In the north/northeast, one ship is loading 12,500 tonnes of bagged sugar in Recife and two more are at large, waiting to load 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar each. In Maceio, two ships are expected to arrive in the next few days.
According to Datanet, exports in the first four months of the 1996/97 crop year which begins in May reached 1.68 million tonnes from the ports of Santos, Paranagua, Antonina and Itajai.
This represented a 29.10 percent increase on the 1.30 million tonnes shipped in the same period last year.
Under the government crop plan, the center-south region is allowed to ship around 3.7 million tonnes overseas free of export tax during the 1996/97 crop year.
But so far only 80 percent of this quota equating to around three million bags has been authorised by the government.
Exporters and producers in the center-south are pushing for the government to release the remaining 20 percent, as they argue they have already used up the initial allowance.
"I would say so far the center-south has exported 2.4 million tonnes and all the line-up that you have at the ports relates to the remaining 600,000 tonnes," one trader said.
Last week, a government official said that the ministry had already prepared a decree authorizing the increase in export tax exemptions and that it may be issued as early as this week.
DataNet consultant Aloisio Sotero thinks it is very possible that the initial center-south quota has already been allocated.
According to the Paranagua port authority, a further 199,326 tonnes were shipped this month up to September 29.

Working on the basis that Santos usually ships substantially more than Paranagua, it would not be surprising if exports by the end of September therefore reached between 2.5 million and 2.6 million tonnnes, Sotero said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
